two_fundamental_gaps_addressed.name: LLMs lack reliable access to clinical data
two_fundamental_gaps_addressed.corti_solution: agents retrieve from trusted external tools at runtime; do not hallucinate; look up + verify + ground on authoritative data

two_fundamental_gaps_addressed.name: LLMs cannot safely act on the world
two_fundamental_gaps_addressed.corti_solution: controlled execution layer; agents plan + invoke tools + multi-step workflows within safety boundaries; pause for human approval + resume only after consent

build_targets: Clinician-facing assistants (documentation editing / guideline lookup / coding & admin support)
Programmatic agent endpoints (embedded in clinical software; triggered by events/APIs/workflows)
Customer-embedded agents (BYO tools; combine Corti + third-party + customer capabilities)
design_principles: Safety First — typed I/O, explicit tool schemas, action guardrails
Memory and Context Management — persistent, multi-context (threads)
Ecosystem of Prebuilt Experts — library of specialized agents
Third-Party Integrations — EHR / CDSS / knowledge bases

definition_of_Expert_PER_CORTI_PUBLIC_DO.note: Corti's public overview describes an Expert as 'specialized agents that connect to data sources, tools, and services'. This is BROADER than iCoDer's charter taxonomy (where Expert = discrete capability, not a full agent). iCoDer will follow its own clean-room taxonomy (Charter §9) but must record this Corti-side definition verbatim.
